newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK property stocks hurt again by intervention fear.
newsitem.headline: HK property stocks hurt again by intervention fear.

text.p: Hong Kong's property stocks were hit for a second day on Friday by concerns that the government may intervene in the property market to stamp out speculation.

The Hang Seng properties sub-index was down 140 points, or 0.54 percent, at 25,737 in mid-morning trade, after sliding to a low of 25,526 earlier. Meanwhile, the Hang Seng index was up 47.86 points to 13,246.
Worldsec International head of research Carlton Poon said "concern that the property market is getting overheated and that the government is forecasting measures" was hurting the sector.
Poon said he was advising clients to sell.
Hong Kong Governor Chris Patten said this week the government was keeping the property market under urgent review.
"Everyone is afraid, somewhat anxious, but I don't think the government can do much," said Priscilla Ng, executive director at CEF GC Brokerage.
Share prices of Cheung Kong, which surged this week following an announcement of a major corporate reshuffle, dropped HK$0.25 to HK$72.0.
Henderson Land slipped HK$0.50 to HK$72.50, New World Development was down HK$0.50 at HK$50.75 and Sun Hung Kai Properties dropped HK$0.25 to HK$92.00.
